Where it began

Ollie Robinson was born in Margate on 1 December 1993 and went to The King's School in Canterbury. He started out at Margate Cricket Club and in Kent's second team, then tried his luck further north. In 2013 he took 59 wickets and scored 1,282 runs in Second XI cricket, a summer that showed he could do more than one thing.

Cricket runs in the family. His stepfather is Paul Farbrace, who became Lancashire's director of cricket.

The player

Sussex took him on in April 2015 on a short deal, because so many of their bowlers were unavailable. He was thrown straight into a Championship match against Durham and, batting at number nine, made a hundred, sharing a Sussex record stand of 164 for the last wicket with Matt Hobden. No Sussex player had made a century on his Championship debut for 95 years. He finished that first season with 46 wickets and the club's young player award.

England picked him in June 2021, against New Zealand, and Tom Latham was his first Test wicket. That summer he took 28 wickets at 19.60, more than any other England bowler, and Wisden made him one of its Cricketers of the Year. He came back strongly in 2026: on his return at Lord's he took three wickets in his first over and 5 for 39, and against Pakistan in August he took eight in the match. By November 2026 he had played 24 Tests and taken 104 wickets at 19.26.

What made him special

He was a medium-pacer rather than a tearaway, and he proved that pace is not everything: five times in Tests he took five wickets in an innings, and each wicket cost him barely nineteen runs. In April 2021, for Sussex against Glamorgan, he took 9 for 78, the best figures by an Englishman since 2016.

His batting never quite matched that debut hundred, and by November 2026 his best in Tests was 58, but he had made two Test fifties, which is two more than plenty of fast bowlers manage.

Away from the middle

Sussex made him vice-captain in 2021 and, in January 2026, captain of their four-day side. After his fine summer of 2026, with 28 wickets in four Tests at 9.30, he was named England Player of the Year by the Cricket Media Club. He has also played in The Hundred for Manchester Originals.

And finally

Sussex signed him because they were short of bowlers. In his first game he batted at number nine and made a hundred. Few emergency signings have answered a question nobody asked quite so well.
